checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in AZ
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
Type I commercial exhaust hood listed/labeled per UL 710 with NFPA 96 compliance and building department-approved capture velocity per IMC 507
ANSUL R-102 (or equivalent UL 300) hood suppression: post-install discharge test certificate + every-6-month cleaning + annual inspection per NFPA 96 §11
ANSUL discharge auto-shutoffs all hood gas + electric fuel sources per IMC 507.7 — use the listed building department source during witness test
Grease interceptor sized per IPC 1003.3.4 by drainage fixture units (4-comp + mop typically 50+ GPM hydromechanical OR 750–1,500 gal exterior gravity); located ≤25 ft developed length from fixtures
Makeup air system balanced to ±10% of hood exhaust per IMC 506.3.4; tempered if > 35°F differential to prevent backdraft
ADA fixture counts per IBC Table 2902.1 + 60 in turning radius + lavatory pipe wrap insulation per ADA §606.5 + mirror reflective edge ≤40 in AFF per ADA §603.3
Local health department food establishment plan review + final inspection sign-off REQUIRED before Certificate of Occupancy (parallel filing — file early)
Walk-in cooler envelope per IECC 403.10.1 (≥R-25 medium-temp panels, ≥R-32 freezer panels); door gasket seal verification at final
Existing sprinkler system reuse: hydraulic recalc for new layout + current 5-year cert per NFPA 25; new heads in cooking equipment area must be K-25+ per NFPA 13
Floor drains within 5 ft of kitchen equipment per IPC 411 with backwater valves where required
Fire alarm + emergency lighting per NFPA 72/101 with current battery capacity test on file
Change of occupancy memo (B/M → A-2): include occupant load + exits + restroom count + sprinkler/fire-alarm impacts per IEBC §1001.2/1001.3 + IBC §303.3 (Group A-2)

Maricopa County (or local equivalent) Environmental Services Department food-establishment plan review + final inspection sign-off REQUIRED before opening — coordinate with City CO schedule (MCESD: maricopa.gov)
Outdoor patio / sidewalk dining: verify city zoning (use permit may apply, e.g. Phoenix ZO §1207); include patio in occupant load + exiting + accessible route + sprinkler/awning review

Phoenix-specific (or equivalent local rule): contractor must be AZ ROC licensed AND associated with the Phoenix SHAPE PHX permit account before submittal (A.R.S. Title 32 Ch. 10) — frequently-missed pre-submittal blocker

Realistic fee warning: a 3,200 sq ft restaurant TI in Phoenix typically lands $8K–$25K+ across plan review + permit + fire + utility + health + zoning. Reject token min-fee outputs; calculate from the live fee schedule before quoting
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City of Phoenix Planning & Development Department (PDD)
response_body.city_contractor_registration: Phoenix requires a separate City Contractor Registration in addition to the Arizona ROC license. Verify the city registration is current before submitting any permit application; an expired or missing city registration can block the permit. Renewal is handled through the City of Phoenix contractor registration process and should be checked before filing.

common_mistakes: Submitting the permit without current Phoenix city contractor registration — Phoenix can reject the application even if the ROC license is valid
Trying to file this as a single trade permit only — a restaurant TI with hood, grease interceptor, panel work, and suppression needs coordinated commercial review
Missing fire suppression submittal details for the hood system — the hood permit and suppression permit are not the same thing
Under-sizing the electrical service or panel for kitchen equipment loads — plan review will flag missing load calculations
Forgetting grease interceptor sizing and fixture count documentation — plumbing review commonly stops the submittal
Starting demolition before the permit is issued and posted — Phoenix can issue stop-work orders and require re-review

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through the City of Phoenix permit/inspection portal associated with PDD. Phoenix requires a minimum 24-hour advance notice; same-day requests are not accepted. Use the city portal for inspection requests and have the permit number ready. Phone: (602) 262-7811. Verify current portal routing on the PDD website before booking.

pro_tips: Check your Phoenix contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are one of the most avoidable rejection reasons.
Phoenix uses a single-permit workflow for some trade combinations, so confirm whether your submittal can be bundled before paying for duplicate filings.
Bring a complete equipment schedule with hood CFM, appliance list, panel schedule, and grease interceptor sizing on the first submittal to avoid correction cycles.
Use the city portal to request inspections at least 24 hours ahead; build that into your schedule so the hood and suppression finals do not stall opening day.
For restaurant TI work, coordinate the hood, suppression, and electrical loads before finalizing the plan set — late equipment changes are what usually blow up plan review.

response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: Commercial restaurant tenant improvements can still be delayed by zoning, use, parking, grease interceptor, and outdoor venting constraints. In Phoenix, verify that the tenant use is allowed in the zoning district and that rooftop or wall exhaust discharge locations comply with zoning and fire code. HOA restrictions are usually not the issue for a commercial tenant space, but landlord approval and any center-specific design criteria can still block the work.
